pillarForecast.why: Keys with dotted lines are his own design and directly fix 'I did not see the exit'; the dotted lines make them hard to miss. Most likely the most praised change, early in the session.
Rocks hurting him was his explicit request and makes the asteroid-field moment real. Small risk that drifting rocks hitting him from off-screen angles feel cheap (P5), not unfair-in-his-favor.

Two hearts plus rocks that hurt plus more starting pursuers stack three difficulty increases at once; early runs may end in arena 1-2 and read as 'too hard' before he adapts. Expect him to adapt within 2-3 runs.

The breathing cadence should give trap-setting room, but 5-7 starting chasers with lull pressure 0.55 is not really calm; he may still find kills accidental, especially in A peaks and in the full-pressure getaway.
The warming border is the kind of designed signal past critics over-credited; he will likely not perceive the cadence as a rhythm, only as unexplained 'suddenly it gets crazy' moments, if at all.
Player-paced arenas of ~10-20s make a full run ~60-110s; he pre-approved shorter levels, but once he wins, the run may feel over too quickly and he may ask for more arenas or something between runs.
Movement only is what he asked for; expect no complaint and possibly no mention at all.

biggestRisk: Front-loaded difficulty: two hearts, rocks that hurt and more pursuers all land together, so run 14 likely ends fast and he spends the remaining runs scrambling for keys under pressure instead of setting traps; the result would echo run 10 ('I just had to escape, kills were accidental') rather than the clever asteroid-field dance the build is aiming for.
abVerdict: Most likely (~55%) he does not name a difference between A and B at all; the warming border and surge timing are subtle. If he does react, lean B (~60/40): calm until he takes a key fits 'set the pace myself', and he would express it as 'I could plan more' or 'it felt more in my control', not by naming the variant. ~20% he proposes a third option (e.g. pressure tied to enemy count or to the exit, or no cadence at all).
